audit_findings.title: Growth may require acquisition spending omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition cash outlays omitted from OE and an acquisition-influenced history may inflate the anchor and the 5%-8% forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s historical growth has depended, and its future growth is likely to continue to depend, in part on its acquisition strategy and the successful integration of acquired businesses into existing operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions contributed to historical growth and are expected to contribute to future growth, while the valuation has no perimeter adjustment or acquisition reinvestment charge. It does not establish how much forecast growth requires acquisitions, so the error amount remains unresolved. The model is materially growth-sensitive: moving from 5% to 0% reduces computed equity value by $205 million or $7.66 per share, and moving from 8% to 0% reduces it by $356 million or $13.33 per share. The acquisition-dependent portion of those differences is unquantified, but it is reasonably capable of materially changing the intrinsic-value range and buy-below conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a 2016-2025 acquisition and organic-growth bridge, including acquired OE and purchase cash outlays, then rerun the anchor and scenarios on a constant organic perimeter or charge the acquisition spending required by each growth case.

audit_findings.title: Pay-as-you-go retiree-health obligation may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.395 million filed obligation; maximum simple bridge effect $0.99 per share; actual incremental effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any future benefit payments exceeding the postretirement expense already retained in equity-level OE would require a bridge deduction or lower forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company funds the cost of these benefits as incurred.
audit_findings.explanation: A missing incremental adjustment is not demonstrated because normalized equity OE retains periodic postretirement expense, and 2025 expense of $1.939 million exceeded the $1.782 million cash payment. Even treating the entire $26.395 million obligation as an additional deduction would reduce value by only about $0.99 per share, equal to 3.9% of bear, 3.0% of base, and 2.5% of bull equity value. After the 30% margin of safety, buy-below would fall by about $0.69, from $23.32 to $22.63, and would not change the conclusion relative to the $75.34 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual forecast benefit payments to the postretirement expense embedded in OE and rerun only for the present value of payments not already captured; confirm the June 2026 current and noncurrent obligation split.

audit_findings.title: Latent LIFO tax claim is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.0 million filed exposure; $0.82 per share maximum simple bridge effect
audit_findings.mechanism: A LIFO liquidation or repeal could create a cash-tax payment not captured by retaining recurring non-cash LIFO expense in OE, requiring a bridge deduction or forecast cash-tax charge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 the Company had a LIFO reserve of $104.6 million, which at the current U.S. Corporate tax rate, represents approximately $22.0 million of income taxes, payment of which is delayed to future dates based upon changes in inventory costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $22.0 million exposure is filed, but payment is contingent and the record does not demonstrate that it will occur or that it is absent from forecast taxes. Even a full immediate deduction would reduce value by about $0.82 per share, or 3.2% of bear, 2.5% of base, and 2.1% of bull equity value. Buy-below would decline by about $0.58 to $22.74, which cannot change the valuation conclusion relative to the $75.34 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether forecast cash taxes or recorded tax liabilities already capture any reversal, then rerun a probability-weighted LIFO-repeal or inventory-liquidation case if evidence indicates payment is probable.

audit_findings.title: Diluted shares combine different measurement dates and may double-count vested awards
audit_findings.magnitude: up to 310,422 shares, 1.16% of the 26.720665 million denominator; maximum approximately 1.18% per-share value increase
audit_findings.mechanism: Awards that vested before June 30, 2026 may already be included in the 26.410243 million outstanding shares, so adding the full December 2025 award balance could overstate diluted shares and understate value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The remaining weighted average vesting period of all non-vested RSUs is 0.7 years as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed measurement dates are demonstrated, but double-counting of any particular award is not established. Even the conservative maximum assumption that all 310,422 awards were duplicated would increase per-share values by only about 1.18%: approximately $0.30 bear, $0.39 base, and $0.46 bull. Buy-below would rise only about $0.27 to $23.59, far below the $75.34 market price, so the issue cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a December 31, 2025-to-June 30, 2026 award roll-forward for grants, vesting, forfeitures and PSU payout levels, remove awards already included in June outstanding shares, and rerun per-share outputs with the date-consistent denominator.
